intro: Data centers use a lot of electricity, and in Louisiana new power plants are being built to supply them. This page tracks what is proposed, who decides, and what it could mean for power bills in New Orleans and Metairie. It is checked by hand against news reports and public filings.

utilities.note: A separate utility with its own rates. The City Council, not the state, approves its power plants and rates.

utilities.parish: Jefferson Parish (Metairie, Kenner, the West Bank)
utilities.note: The same utility building the power plants for Meta's data center, so the LPSC's decisions on those plants can affect its customers' rates.

projects.name: Meta Hyperion data center
projects.power: 3 gas plants, about 2,262 MW, approved in 2025; 7 more, about 5,278 MW, proposed in 2026
projects.status: Phase 1 plants under construction: two in Richland Parish (late 2028) and one at Entergy's Waterford site in St. Charles Parish (by the end of 2029). The 7-plant expansion (4 in Richland, 3 in Pointe Coupee Parish), with batteries and new transmission lines, is in LPSC docket U-37882, with a vote expected in December 2026.

projects.name: Hut 8 River Bend campus
projects.power: 330 MW from Entergy Louisiana for the first lease, with room for up to 1,000 MW more
projects.status: Under construction. A 15-year, 245 MW lease to Fluidstack, backed by Google; later reporting describes the capacity as built for Anthropic. First data hall due in the second quarter of 2027.

projects.name: New Orleans East proposal
projects.where: Near I-10 and Read Boulevard, New Orleans
projects.status: Withdrawn. The developer pulled its zoning permit hours after the City Council's January 28, 2026 vote to pause data centers.

timeline.what: Approves Entergy Louisiana's three gas plants, about 2,262 MW, to power Meta's Richland Parish data center.
Adopts the "Lightning" directive, 4-1: power plants for very large customers can skip competitive bidding, with a decision due within about eight months.
Votes 6-0 to pause data centers (and crypto mining) citywide for a year while the City Planning Commission writes zoning rules.
Votes 4-1 to fast-track Entergy Louisiana's application for seven more gas plants for Meta.
Adopts its first data center zoning: industrial districts only, a 300-foot buffer from homes and schools, and a noise cap. In April it had rejected an eight-month moratorium, 5-3.

Recommend banning the largest data centers (over 100,000 sq ft and 20 MW) citywide and allowing smaller ones in some districts, subject to review by Entergy New Orleans and the Sewerage and Water Board.
Votes 3-1 to overturn a judge's order that Meta provide its job and power-demand figures in the expansion case.
Votes 5-2 against the staff recommendation and extends the suspension, asking for more information and community input.
Sue the LPSC in state court, arguing the Lightning directive was adopted without proper public notice.

next: December 2026: the LPSC is expected to vote on the seven-plant expansion for Meta (reports give December 10 or 16; check docket U-37882).

bills.text: Meta's contract covers the full cost of serving it, and the agreement is projected to produce net savings for other customers over 20 years.

Consumer and environmental groups (the Alliance for Affordable Energy, the Union of Concerned Scientists, Earthjustice) argue that fuel and some transmission costs are spread to all customers, and that customers could be left paying for the plants if Meta leaves early.
